svg.title: How the tests run lcw now
svg.desc: How the tests run lcw now. A prepared git repository is made once per test process and each test gets a fresh copy. Test files call cli(), which runs an lcw command inside the test process, one at a time, through the command line's main(), now callable, and gets back the printed text and exit code. The status line is drawn in the test process with a clean environment; a shell starts only for its shell script. Real-process tests still start node lcw.mjs as a separate program, for each family of commands, a lock race, a lock left by a dead process, a background merge --wait and the spend and quota runners, and compare its output with cli(); if they differ the test fails and names the command. The spend runner now hooks its stop handlers before it starts the command.
svg.text: How the tests run lcw now

g.text: 1 of 3 · The usual test: an lcw command runs in-process, in a fresh copy of the prepared repository
2 of 3 · A real-process test: the same commands through the lcw program and through cli(), compared
3 of 3 · A failure: the two outputs differ, so the test fails and names the command
Three stories play in turn: the usual test, a real-process test, and a failure.
